subject: Architecture
title: Mass Timber: Skyscrapers Made of Wood
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mass Timber: Skyscrapers Made of Wood.

hook.text: Engineers are building skyscrapers from wood — not because they're nostalgic, but because wood beats steel on carbon.

buildup.text: Cross-laminated timber layers wood at right angles — creating panels as strong as steel but six times lighter.

discovery.text: Trees absorb carbon while growing. Using wood in buildings locks that carbon away for the building's lifetime.

twist.text: Thick mass timber chars on the outside during fire but doesn't burn through — it's actually safer than steel beams.

climax.text: Milwaukee's Ascent tower is 25 stories of mass timber — the tallest timber building in the world in 2022.

punchline.text: The oldest building material. Now the newest skyscraper technology.

quiz.question: Why is mass timber considered better for the climate than steel?
options: It requires less water to manufacture
Trees absorb carbon, and using wood locks it in the building
Timber factories produce zero pollution during manufacturing
